content:
Elena: Quick sync — after the launch we have 12 customer-reported issues, ~8 UI/UX bugs, 4 backend SLO regressions, and 6 enhancement requests. Need a quick callout on what gets a hotfix vs next minor.
Rahul: TL;DR — hotfix = anything causing data loss, broken auth, or >1% error rate regression. UI polish and minor perf can wait.
Marta: +1. Can we get the top 3 customer-impact bugs triaged now? I can own the bug queue for the hotfix cut.
Sam: I put a tentative list in the backlog board: https://redwood/boards/launch-1. Top three flagged are: 1) session restore failing on long contexts, 2) streaming truncated responses for >2k tokens, 3) session-scoped prompts not persisted.
Priya: For scoring, propose: severity (user-facing impact), frequency (reported by X customers), lift (dev days). We should compute a quick score and sort.
Diego: I ran a quick query: session restore errors = 14 incidents (3 customers), stream truncation = 6 incidents (5 customers), prompt persistence = 2 incidents (1 customer). Also there are 2 infra regressions causing 5-10% tail latency spikes.
Elena: Good data. My suggested rule: include any issue that is (severity >= high AND frequency >= medium) OR any regression increasing 95p latency > 10%.
Rahul: Agree. That would pull session restore and tail latency regressions into hotfix. Stream truncation — borderline but customer-visible.
Marta: If we include stream truncation in the hotfix, we need a rollback plan in case it regresses other streaming fixes. Can engineering do a quick canary?
Diego: Yes — we can roll a canary to 5% of traffic for the hotfix branch and monitor token-level errors and 95p latency. I can set up a canary config by EOD.
Sam: Timebox: hotfix branch cut tomorrow morning. Engineering estimates: session restore = 1.5 dev days, tail latency fix = 2 dev days (profiling + rollout), streaming fix = 2.5 dev days. QA+canary = 1 day. Total ~7 days.
Priya: That fits an urgent patch cycle. For the enhancement asks (embedding caching, per-route quotas, improved prompt templates), we should slot into next minor (3-week cycle) and mark owners.
Elena: Decision: Hotfix will include session restore, tail-latency regression mitigations, and streaming truncation only if Diego's initial canary shows no additional regressions at 5%. All UI polish/enhancements go to minor release.
Rahul: Action items: Marta to open hotfix tickets with priority P0/P1 and acceptance criteria; Diego to create canary config and monitoring dashboards; Sam to schedule patch cut and communicate to support; Priya to update roadmap and notify the top affected customers.
Marta: I just created the tickets: HOTFIX-101 (session-restore) HOTFIX-102 (tail-latency) HOTFIX-103 (stream-truncate-canary). Added repro steps and minimal acceptance tests.
Diego: Canary dashboard: https://redwood/dashboards/hotfix-177777. Will alert on 5xxs, truncation count, 95p latency.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary cluster allocation requested — 5% traffic.
Sam: Support message drafted and queued for tomorrow morning: short notice, rollback plan, expected timeline.
Priya: I'll email the top 6 affected customers with planned timeline and will include the workaround for session restore (manual session export/import).
Elena: Great. Follow-on: after hotfix closes, we'll run a grooming session to prioritize the 6 enhancement asks into the next minor. Tentative meeting Friday 9:30am PT.
Rahul: One more thing — add an eval harness to prevent regressions on stream truncation in CI. Can someone pair with QA?
Marta: I'll pair with QA for that test.
Diego: I'll add token-boundary unit tests and a lightweight reference runner in CI.
Elena: Thanks everyone. I'll check back after canary is live. :thumbsup:
Priya: Thanks — will update roadmap and the customer comms channel.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started at 1777771200 for HOTFIX branch.
